test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 19 Sept, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: AB is a chord of length 32 cm of a circle of radius 20 cm, the tangents at A and B intersect at a point T. Find length TA (rounded off to two digits after decimal).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Length of the tangent = (Radius × Half of chord) ÷ Distance of chord from the center

Distance of chord from center = √(Radius² − Half-chord²) = √(20² − 16²) = 12 cm

Length of Tangent TA = (20 × 16) ÷ 12

TA = 320 ÷ 12 = 80 ÷ 3 = 26.67 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 26.67 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the circle (OA) = 20 cm

Length of the chord (AB) = 32 cm

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the line joining the center O and point T intersect the chord AB at point M.

⇒ The line from the center to the intersection of two tangents is the perpendicular bisector of the chord joining the points of tangency.

⇒ AM = AB ÷ 2 = 32 ÷ 2 = 16 cm.

⇒ In right-angled ΔOMA, using the Pythagoras theorem:

⇒ OM = √(OA² − AM²) = √(20² − 16²)

⇒ OM = √(400 − 256) = √144 = 12 cm.

⇒ In right-angled triangles ΔOMA and ΔOAT:

⇒ ∠AOM is common to both triangles.

⇒ ∠OMA = 90° (Since OT is perpendicular to AB)

⇒ ∠OAT = 90° (The radius to the point of tangency is perpendicular to the tangent)

⇒ ∴ ΔOMA ∼ ΔOAT (By AA similarity criterion).

⇒ The ratio of their corresponding sides will be proportional:

⇒ AM ÷ OM = TA ÷ OA

⇒ 16 ÷ 12 = TA ÷ 20

⇒ TA = (16 × 20) ÷ 12 = 320 ÷ 12

⇒ TA = 80 ÷ 3 = 26.666... ≈ 26.67 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 26.67 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Tangents to a Circle

A tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact. The lengths of two tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are always equal.

Perpendicular Bisector of a Chord

The perpendicular line drawn from the center of a circle to a chord bisects the chord into two equal halves. Conversely, a straight line drawn through the center to bisect a chord is always perpendicular to it.

Secant-Tangent Theorem

If a tangent segment and a secant segment are drawn to a circle from an exterior point, then the square of the tangent length equals the product of the external secant length and the total secant length.
